# `get_annotate_result`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Return the cached annotation result for one image (default: the latest).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ) except that its relay condition omits the two newest model checks) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ (handler); unresolved (result members) |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb74f0, GetAnnotateResult @0x1fce80 (64-bit build); 32-bit handler compared statically; the 32-bit relay condition lacks the S30Plus/S80 board checks but reaches the same relay helpers; firmware 9.75 member from the 9.75 reports |

Looks up the cached annotation object for the requested image id and returns it unchanged; it starts no computation. Under some secondary-camera and view-mode conditions the original request is first forwarded to the secondary process (relay failure behaviour is unresolved). Although it is a read, every call writes log state, so the strict grade is MUTATOR; the observer tier is B. The members of the cached object are not enumerated by the evidence. Whether a matching annotation event exists is unresolved; current activity is reported by the annotate member of the app state. Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0: the keyed form accepts file_path, so a stored file can be annotated; the call goes through the relay-only form of the relay check (no 203 or 524), with errors 102 and 105 on the new member.

Side effects: Reads the cached annotation map; the helper logs default-id selection and the success, empty and not-found branches (shared log state). May forward the request to the secondary process. No hardware or setting change.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_annotate_result"`. [READ] |
| `params` | integer\|array\|object | no | most recent image | Optional. Omitted, an empty array or an object without img_id selects the most recent image (internal sentinel 65535). A supplied id must be 0..65534; 65535 and negative values are rejected with 204. Unknown object keys are ignored. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | img_id present but not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 204 | img_id outside 0..65534 | `out of limit` |
| 207 | No cached annotation data, or the cached object is flagged empty | `fail to operate` |
| 102 | Firmware 9.75: file_path invalid | `invalid argument` |
| 105 | Firmware 9.75: file_path is not a string | `expected string` |
| 200 | Requested (or default) image id not found in the cache; also the dispatcher case where the request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Failures while forwarding to the secondary process are unresolved. No result member on errors. Firmware 9.75: 203 and 524 are not newly reachable: the relay check is the relay-only form without occupancy probes (a prior statement that they are is withdrawn).

## Example

Request, latest - Latest image:

```json
{"id":45,"method":"get_annotate_result"}
```

Request, by-id - Keyed form:

```json
{"id":46,"method":"get_annotate_result","params":{"img_id":3}}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_annotate_result","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"id":47}
```
